dataset_family: Ferrara / San Giovanni Rotondo memory-clinic MCI series: S. Anna University Hospital, Ferrara and Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, San Giovanni Rotondo (Italy), 2006-2018; 620 MCI enrolled, 462 followed (median 33 months), 190 converters. The same two-clinic family yields other corpus papers (e.g. P-1237, P-1223), which would count once with this one
method_family: Evidence type for VF-27: a baseline GDS-15 score compared between converters and stable MCI (Mann-Whitney), plus a univariate Cox model on three GDS strata, in a longitudinal memory-clinic prognosis cohort; the paper's primary method is Cox regression with a dichotomised prognostic score. This is closely similar to P-647 (baseline GDS plus Cox in a longitudinal MCI cohort)
what_it_shows: In 462 MCI patients followed for a median of 33 months, GDS-15 severity strata (5-10 and >10 versus 0-4) were not associated with progression to dementia in univariate Cox regression (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.50-1.11; HR 0.85, 0.47-1.54, p = 0.35). Adding GDS to the multivariable model did not change the results. But the continuous baseline GDS was significantly LOWER in converters than in stable patients (median 3 vs 5, p = 0.007): an inverse association, not a null. Amnestic MCI patients also had fewer depressive symptoms than non-amnestic ones (4 vs 5, p = 0.05) and converted more often, which may account for the inverse difference. There is no brain-measure correlation with GDS, and all participants have MCI.
why: Zuliani et al., Aging Clin Exp Res 2021;33:1895-1902. The PDF title and authors match the summaries.md block and the map entry (DOI 10.1007/s40520-020-01697-8). The block never mentions GDS; everything below is from the PDF. The table footnotes expand GDS as 'global deterioration scale', but the methods say '15 items geriatric depression scale' and the /15 range confirms the depression scale. Against Table A1: the stratified Cox result supports the conversion limb in the sense that a higher depression-severity stratum carried no higher risk. The Table A1 wording, however, is that continuous severity scores 'fail to track' conversion, and here the continuous score did track conversion, in the inverse direction and significantly (p = 0.007): converters had fewer depressive symptoms. That fits the ledger's 'the milder stratum sometimes carried the worse signal' better than the Table A1 'fail to track' wording. Hence 'partly'. The part it shows: depression severity did not grade prognosis upward; the stratified Cox HRs were null and below 1. It does NOT show: the first clause (all participants have MCI), the brain-measures limb (MRI/CT findings were only tabulated against outcome, never against GDS), or the 'although' clause. Limits: GDS is a covariate, not the study's focus; the multivariable adjustment for GDS is 'data not shown'; the 5-10 stratum p value is missing from Table 3 in the extract, though its CI crosses 1; 158 of 620 were lost to follow-up; the outcome is all-cause dementia. Independence: no shared sample, site or authors with P-643 (Korea University Guro) or P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort), and none with the other candidates. P-788 cites this paper, but they share no data. The registry Dataset field names only Ferrara, but the PDF shows two sites (Ferrara and San Giovanni Rotondo). Method-family caution: the depression evidence is a baseline-scale plus Cox analysis, like P-647's.

Anna University Hospital, Ferrara (Italy) or of the Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, San Giovanni Rotondo (Italy) in which the diagnosis of MCI was made. After the initial examination and diagnosis, 158 subjects were lost during follow-up
